name: Turn this week's news on your topics into content ideas in Google Sheets with one AI agent and looot

parameters.content:
## Weekly content ideas from what moved in your topics

### How it works
1. Every Monday at 8, **Topics** hands the agent your themes and audience.
2. One AI agent searches this week's news per topic, pulls Google autocomplete suggestions for the search terms people type, and reads the two most useful articles, all through looot.
3. It writes content ideas with a title, an angle, why it matters now, target keywords and sources.
4. Each idea lands as a row in Google Sheets.

One looot credential replaces the SerpAPI and Firecrawl accounts this flow usually needs.

**Cost per run**, from looot's public catalog on 2026-10-31: news search $0.001, Google autocomplete $0.00099, a page read from $0.0002. Three topics cost about $0.01 in data. Each call is capped at $0.03 and the agent at 25 steps, so a run can never spend more than $0.75. Model tokens are billed by OpenAI.

### Setup
- Needs the verified community node **n8n-nodes-looot** (built against 0.1.4): Settings > Community nodes > Install, search `looot`. [Install guide](https://docs.n8n.io/integrations/community-nodes/installation/verified-install/)
- looot: sign up at [looot.ai](https://looot.ai), top up (from $5), create an agent token under Settings > Agent tokens, then add a **looot API** credential in n8n.
- Google Sheets and OpenAI credentials.
- A sheet named Ideas with the headers: week, topic, title, angle, why_now, keywords, sources, cost_usd. Set its ID in **Save ideas**.
- Edit **Topics**.
- Self-hosted n8n: set `N8N_COMMUNITY_PACKAGES_ALLOW_TOOL_USAGE=true` so the agent can use the looot node as a tool.

### Customization
Ask for LinkedIn post drafts instead of titles in the system message. Run it daily for news-heavy topics.

options.systemMessage:
You plan content for a B2B brand.
For each topic:
1. job:news.search with {"query": "<topic>"} and keep stories from the last 7 days.
2. job:google.keywords.suggestions with {"query": "<topic>"} to see what people type.
3. Read the two most useful articles with job:web.scrape.markdown.
Then write the ideas: a specific title, the angle, why now in one sentence (cite the news), 3 to 5 keywords from the suggestions, and the source URLs. No generic ideas.

parameters.toolDescription:
Runs one looot data call and returns the run: status, result and actualCost. Every call is capped. Use only these ids and inputs:
- job:news.search, input {"query": "..."}: Google News articles.
- job:google.keywords.suggestions, input {"query": "..."}: Google autocomplete suggestions.
- job:web.scrape.markdown, input {"url": "https://..."}: one page as text.
